scope: Enumerate per-case handlers of CharaElement::vftable[8] async event dispatcher (FUN_0058E0C0, already cataloged by the element-vtable8-bulk pass). 1519-byte switch on param_2 covering 21 distinct sub-opcodes 0x4A..0x64. Catalog the per-case leaf handler functions.

method.step1: Decomp FUN_0058E0C0 via DumpFunctionDecomp.java. Confirms 1519B switch with 21 distinct cases: 0x4A/0x4E/0x4F/0x50/0x51/0x53/0x54/0x55/0x56/0x57/0x58/0x59/0x5A/0x5B/0x5C/0x5D/0x5E/0x5F/0x60/0x61/0x64.
method.step2: Classify cases by structure: 9 INLINE state writes (0x4A flag clear, 0x4E + 0x4F bulk struct writes of 32B each, 0x5C 16B write, 0x5D/0x5E/0x5F/0x60/0x61 single-field writes); 10 LEAF handlers (0x53/0x54/0x55/0x56/0x57/0x58/0x59/0x5A/0x5B/0x64) each calling a dedicated helper function; 2 COMPLEX cases (0x50 lookup-and-cleanup pair; 0x51 action-state-async-transition with c2s 0x00CA emit via FUN_004D6D10).
method.step3: Cross-reference the c2s 0x00CA emit path in case 0x51 against the chara-action-state-pipeline pass (FUN_0058A090 tick processor also emits c2s 0x00CA via FUN_00589030) and the c2s-remaining-emitters pass (FUN_004D6D10 thunk = BCS-Y-0323). Two distinct paths to c2s 0x00CA from CharaElement: SYNC via slot 9 / FUN_0058B2A0 / FUN_0058A090 tick (FUN_00589030); ASYNC via slot 8 / FUN_0058E0C0 case 0x51 inline (FUN_004D6D10 thunk + FUN_004DD620 builder).

key_findings: FUN_0058E0C0 is CharaElement::vftable[8] async event dispatcher (already cataloged by the element-vtable8-bulk pass). 1519 bytes, switch on param_2 covering 21 sub-opcodes in the 0x4A..0x64 range. Larger than the 17-case estimate in the plan.

Case 0x51 is the architecturally significant one: ASYNCHRONOUS action-state transition path that EMITS c2s 0x00CA UpdatePlayerPosition via FUN_004D6D10 (BCS-Y-0323 short-body thunk) + FUN_004DD620 (position builder). This is a SECOND path to c2s 0x00CA from CharaElement, parallel to the chara-action-state-pipeline pass's SYNC tick-processor path (FUN_0058A090 -> FUN_00589030). Confirms the dual-emit nature of position updates: tick-driven (sync) vs event-driven (async).
Cases 0x4E and 0x4F are 32-byte struct writes (4 qwords each) into actor record at +0x224..+0x244 and +0x244..+0x264 - likely transform matrices, bone orientations, or animation pose state.

Case 0x50 does an actor lookup via FUN_004D9970 (cataloged actor-by-id resolver from client-architecture 'S2C dispatch has five architectural patterns') and conditional cleanup via FUN_004DD9D0 - likely a target-actor-validate-then-detach operation.
Cases 0x55 calls a vtable slot at *(this+0xBA0)+0x2C - this is a virtual call on an embedded sub-object; the sub-object class is currently unknown without further drilling.

Case 0x64 (decimal 100) is a 3-step path: build context via FUN_00585800 -> populate buffer via FUN_00587370 -> dispatch via FUN_005901D0. Likely a log-entry or event-history builder. Distinct shape from other cases.

Pattern note: CharaElement slots 8 and 9 BOTH dispatch sub-opcodes from packet payload but use DIFFERENT mechanisms. Slot 9 (FUN_0058CCA0) uses an outer case-table (0x0F / 0xCC / 0xCD / 0xCE / 0xCF / 0xD0..0xE5 / 0x134 / etc - matches the actor cluster Pattern B opcode range) and routes to per-case sub-dispatchers like FUN_0058B2A0. Slot 8 (FUN_0058E0C0) uses a different case range (0x4A..0x64) which does NOT correspond to wire opcodes - these are internal sub-event types delivered via the async queue (BCS-S-0048/0049 Sqex::Thread::Queue<MainPacket>).
